headline: ACC probes money laundering allegations against Asif Mahmud
summary: The Anti-Corruption Commission has launched an investigation into claims that the former interim government advisor laundered billions of taka abroad.
details: The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) is investigating allegations of massive corruption and money laundering against former interim government Youth and Sports Advisor Asif Mahmud Sajeeb Bhuyan.

According to ACC Assistant Director Mohammad Tanjir Ahmed, the probe includes claims of taking commissions for appointments and transfers, including 60 crore BDT for a Dhaka North City Corporation administrator and 2-10 crore BDT for 36 District Commissioners.

The ACC is also looking into allegations of tender commissions (10-30%) in the Dhaka South City Corporation and the Ministry of Local Government, as well as irregularities in the Sayedabad Water Treatment Plant and Sheikh Russel Mini Stadium projects.
The most striking claims involve money laundering to Dubai (4,500 crore BDT), Singapore (3,000 crore BDT), Australia (2,000 crore BDT), and Switzerland (1,500 crore BDT), totaling 11,000 crore BDT.
The ACC further alleges that these funds were used to purchase luxury villas and invest in businesses abroad, with some transactions reportedly made through relatives.
Asif Mahmud has denied the allegations and previously warned of legal action if the ACC did not retract statements regarding 'primary truth' in the claims.
Responding to the latest press conference on Facebook, Mahmud sarcastically remarked, 'If you find anything abroad during the investigation, just give me 10%, I'm struggling to get by.'
caption:
11,000 crore BDT laundered abroad? The ACC is probing massive corruption claims against former advisor Asif Mahmud.

The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) is investigating allegations of massive corruption and money laundering against former interim government Youth and Sports Advisor Asif Mahmud Sajeeb Bhuyan.

According to ACC Assistant Director Mohammad Tanjir Ahmed, the probe includes claims of taking commissions for appointments and transfers, including 60 crore BDT for a Dhaka North City Corporation administrator and 2-10 crore BDT for 36 District Commissioners.

The ACC is also looking into allegations of tender commissions (10-30%) in the Dhaka South City Corporation and the Ministry of Local Government, as well as irregularities in the Sayedabad Water Treatment Plant and Sheikh Russel Mini Stadium projects.

The most striking claims involve money laundering to Dubai (4,500 crore BDT), Singapore (3,000 crore BDT), Australia (2,000 crore BDT), and Switzerland (1,500 crore BDT), totaling 11,000 crore BDT.

The ACC further alleges that these funds were used to purchase luxury villas and invest in businesses abroad, with some transactions reportedly made through relatives.

Asif Mahmud has denied the allegations and previously warned of legal action if the ACC did not retract statements regarding 'primary truth' in the claims.

Responding to the latest press conference on Facebook, Mahmud sarcastically remarked, 'If you find anything abroad during the investigation, just give me 10%, I'm struggling to get by.'

headline: NCP names mayoral candidates for Dhaka city corporations
summary: Asif Mahmud Sajeeb Bhuiyan will contest for Dhaka North and Nasiruddin Patwari for Dhaka South.
details: The National Citizens Party (NCP) has officially announced its mayoral candidates for the upcoming Dhaka North and South City Corporation elections.
Asif Mahmud Sajeeb Bhuiyan has been nominated for the Dhaka North City Corporation, while Nasiruddin Patwari will contest for the Dhaka South City Corporation.
The announcement was made by Nahid Islam, the party's convener and Chief Whip of the opposition in the National Parliament, during a meeting at the NCP office in Banglamotor, Dhaka.
During the meeting, party leaders discussed organizational preparations at the ward level, the selection of potential councillor candidates, and various civic issues facing the capital city.
Nahid Islam provided overall guidance to party leaders on identifying ward-based civic problems and mobilizing movements to address them.
The party also emphasized maintaining constant communication and support for the families of those martyred or injured during the July uprising.
Additionally, the NCP directed its members to maintain ward-based surveillance and prevention against any subversive activities by members of the Awami League.
The meeting was attended by senior leaders including Ariful Islam Adib, convener for Dhaka North, and Ishaq Sarkar, convener for Dhaka South.
caption:
Asif Mahmud and Nasiruddin Patwari to lead NCP's bid for Dhaka's mayoral seats.

The National Citizens Party (NCP) has officially announced its mayoral candidates for the upcoming Dhaka North and South City Corporation elections.

Asif Mahmud Sajeeb Bhuiyan has been nominated for the Dhaka North City Corporation, while Nasiruddin Patwari will contest for the Dhaka South City Corporation.

The announcement was made by Nahid Islam, the party's convener and Chief Whip of the opposition in the National Parliament, during a meeting at the NCP office in Banglamotor, Dhaka.

During the meeting, party leaders discussed organizational preparations at the ward level, the selection of potential councillor candidates, and various civic issues facing the capital city.

Nahid Islam provided overall guidance to party leaders on identifying ward-based civic problems and mobilizing movements to address them.

The party also emphasized maintaining constant communication and support for the families of those martyred or injured during the July uprising.

Additionally, the NCP directed its members to maintain ward-based surveillance and prevention against any subversive activities by members of the Awami League.

The meeting was attended by senior leaders including Ariful Islam Adib, convener for Dhaka North, and Ishaq Sarkar, convener for Dhaka South.
